NEW DELHI: Indian para-javelin star Navdeep Singh has credited the support and training facilities at the Sports Authority of India’s (SAI) Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) Stadium in New Delhi for helping the country’s para-athletes deliver a historic performance at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games.India finished fourth in the continental competition with a record 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — its best-ever haul at the Games. Para athletics led the charge with 65 medals, including 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze.Navdeep won bronze in the men’s javelin throw F40/F41 on Friday, improving on his fourth-place finish at the 2022 edition. The Paris Paralympics gold medallist said training alongside fellow athletes at the JLN Stadium’s main track helped him prepare for the competition environment in Aichi-Nagoya.“Most of us Asian Games-bound athletes, including me, did our preparations at the JLN Stadium for the Asian Games 2026,” said Navdeep after his medal win. “This allowed us to acclimatise and get the feel. Despite the ongoing [Indian Super League] football matches, they kept the Asian Games a priority, which I felt was quite impressive, and that supported me,” he added.Navdeep also highlighted how access to the main track allowed athletes across disciplines to focus on their preparations without unnecessary delays.“Sprinters need an empty track, so they got a good chance to train inside it. I majorly train at the SAI Regional Centres [Bengaluru, Sonipat and Gandhinagar], where there is not much crowd and I don’t have to wait for other athletes to finish their throws. This all happened here at the JLN Stadium too. I could focus on my preparations rather than focusing on rotations and waiting for my turn,” Navdeep said, expressing hopes of returning to the JLN Stadium for the next season.A total of 14 para-athletics medallists from the Aichi-Nagoya Games trained at the JLN Stadium ahead of the competition. More than 50 other para-athletes also train at the facility.The athletes who trained at the facility delivered medals across track and field events. Gold medallists included Praveen Kumar in the men’s high jump T64, Sandeep Kumar in the men’s 400m T64, where he set a world record, Pranav Soorma in the men’s club throw F51, Rinku Hooda in the men’s javelin throw F46, and Simran Sharma, who won the women’s 100m and 200m T12 titles, setting Games records in both events.The silver medallists included Manjeet, Nimisha Chakkungalparambil, Varun Singh Bhati, Preeti Pal and Ajeet Singh Yadav. Bronze medallists included Sandeep Kumar in the men’s 100m T44, Sandip Sanjay Sargar in the men’s javelin combined classification event, Navdeep in the men’s javelin F40/F41 and Anubhav Choudhary in the men’s 100m T35.The medal-winning performances highlighted the contribution of the JLN Stadium’s training environment to India’s record campaign at the Asian Para Games.
Article Summary: India finished fourth in the continental competition with a record 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze. Para athletics led the charge with 65 medals, including 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. Navdeep Singh won bronze in the men’s javelin throw F40/F41 on Friday.

Article Title: India script history with best-ever haul of 114 medals as nine golds cap golden day at Asian Para Games

NEW DELHI: India's para-athletes produced a spectacular finish to their campaign at the Asian Para Games, registering their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals, including 30 gold, after a record-breaking final-day flourish in Aichi-Nagoya on Friday.India collected nine gold medals on the day — their biggest single-day haul of the ongoing edition — with champions emerging from badminton, archery, shooting and athletics. The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023.The achievement was particularly significant as India competed with a contingent of 168 athletes, nearly half the size of the squad that represented the country in Hangzhou.India remained fourth in the standings at the end of its campaign, although the final positions could change after a few remaining events on Saturday.Athletics remained India's biggest medal contributor, accounting for 65 medals, 12 more than at the previous edition. On Friday, however, the spotlight was shared with a superb badminton campaign and gold-winning performances in shooting and archery. Star javelin thrower Sumit Antil led an Indian 1-2-3 finish in the men's F42-44/61-64 combined event . The reigning Paralympic and world champion threw 72.46m to defend his title, while Mahendra Gurjar took silver with 59.03m and Sandip Sanjay Sargar claimed bronze with 64.48m. Gurjar finished ahead of Sargar on Raza points, which determine rankings in combined-classification events.Pranav Soorma added another gold in the men's club throw F51, defending his title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m. Dharambir secured bronze with 27.71m.Sandeep delivered a world-record performance in the men's 400m T64, clocking 52.28 seconds for gold. India's Ajay Kumar also reached the podium, winning bronze in a Games-record time of 53.61 seconds.Haney produced another world record, throwing 60.49m to win the men's javelin F37/38 title. India also picked up silver medals through Nimisha Chakkungalparambil in the women's long jump T47 and Parmod Bijarnia in the men's 1500m T46, where he clocked 4:09.65.India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar and Games debutant Naveen Sivakumar.Nitesh defeated compatriot and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in the men's singles SL3 final. He later added a silver medal in mixed doubles SL3-SU5 alongside Thulasimathi Murugesan.Naveen, meanwhile, defeated Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 to win the men's singles SL4 title. Thulasimathi enjoyed a memorable campaign of her own , combining with Manasi Joshi to win gold in women's doubles SL3-SU5. The Indian pair beat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final.The 24-year-old also secured silver in women's singles SU5 after losing 18-21, 11-21 to Yang in the final, completing a three-medal haul.Shooter Mona Agarwal added another golden chapter to India's campaign, shattering the world record to win the women's 50m rifle 3 positions SH1 title with a score of 357.5 points.The 38-year-old had earlier won the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 gold with a Games-record score of 250.0 points, edging compatriot Avani Lekhara, who took silver with 249.6.Mona's latest triumph gave her a second gold of the Games and further underlined her standing among India's leading para-shooters. She had also secured India's first 2028 Paralympic quota earlier this year.In archery, Paralympic champion Harvinder Singh teamed up with debutant Vijay Sundi to win the men's recurve doubles gold, defeating China's Yun Duo and Zhao Lixue 5-1 in the final.India's women's recurve doubles pair of Bhawna Choudhary and Pooja Jatyan settled for silver after losing 0-6 to China's Gao Zihan and Wang Xueqian.India's swimmers also exceeded expectations, finishing the Games with 11 medals, including three silver. Himanshu Nandal completed a hat-trick of bronze medals by finishing third in the men's 100m freestyle S11. The 22-year-old, who was born blind due to optic nerve failure, clocked 1:05.90, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita (58.22) and China's Chuanzhen Sun (58.70).Nandal had earlier won bronze in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. Ravi Budigina also finished with three medals, comprising two silver and one bronze.With nine gold medals on Friday and a record overall haul of 114, India signed off from its Asian Para Games campaign with its most successful performance at the continental event, surpassing the benchmark set in Hangzhou three years ago.
Article Summary: India's para-athletes produced a spectacular finish to their campaign at the Asian Para Games. The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023. India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Sumit Antil leads India's javelin 1-2-3 as Pranav Soorma strikes gold again

Sumit Antil leads India's javelin sweep

NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a golden double in para-athletics at the Asian Para Games on Friday, with star javelin thrower Sumit Antil leading a podium sweep and Pranav Soorma defending his title in the men's club throw F51 event.Antil successfully defended his gold in the men's javelin throw F42-44/61-64 combined event, while Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar completed an all-Indian podium finish. Soorma, meanwhile, added another gold to his collection with a Games-record performance in the club throw.The results added to India's medal haul as the country's para-athletes continued to deliver strong performances in Aichi-Nagoya.The 28-year-old Antil, a two-time Paralympic gold medallist and world record holder, produced a best throw of 72.46m in his second attempt to claim gold.Although he could not surpass his personal best, Antil was comfortably ahead of the field while competing in the F64 classification. He had won gold at the 2023 Asian Para Games with a then-world-record throw of 73.29m before improving the mark to 74.82m in May this year.Gurjar secured silver with a throw of 59.03m, while Sargar took bronze with an effort of 64.48m.Despite Sargar recording the longer distance, Gurjar finished ahead because of his superior Raza points score, which is used to determine rankings in combined events involving athletes from different classifications.The F42, F44, F62 and F64 categories are combined in certain field events, including javelin and discus throw, to create a larger and more competitive field. The classifications cover athletes with lower-limb impairments, with some competing without prostheses and others using them.Soorma continued India's gold rush by successfully defending his men's club throw F51 title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m.The Indian had won gold in the same event at the previous edition of the Asian Para Games and claimed silver at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.South Korea's Jiwon Jung took silver with a personal-best throw of 28.40m, while Dharamvir secured bronze with 27.71m to give India another double podium finish.The F51 classification is for athletes with significant movement limitations affecting the trunk, legs and hands, with varying degrees of impairment in arm movement. Competitors perform their throws from a seated position.With Antil leading a historic Indian sweep in the javelin and Soorma retaining his title, India's para-athletes delivered another memorable day in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: Sumit Antil leads India's javelin sweep at the Asian Para Games. Pranav Soorma defends his title in the men's club throw F51 event. Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar complete all-Indian podium finish.

NEW DELHI: Double gold medallists Mona Agarwal and Nishad Kumar will be India's flag-bearers at the closing ceremony of the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Saturday, following outstanding campaigns in shooting and para-athletics.Both athletes won two gold medals each at the continental event, with Mona producing a record-breaking performance in shooting and Nishad excelling in the high jump and long jump.Their selection as flag-bearers recognises their achievements as India prepare to bring the Games to a close.The 38-year-old Mona opened India's medal account in shooting by winning gold in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event with a Games-record score of 250.0 points. His right arm was severed by a grass-cutting machine at his family's farm in Himachal Pradesh when he was six years old. Article Title: Who is Himanshu Nandal? The para-swimmer who won a hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games in Japan
Article Text:
Himanshu Nandal (PTI Photo)

Who is Himanshu Nandal?

From Paris Paralympics qualification to Asian Para Games medals

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal made his mark at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, completing a hat-trick of bronze medals with another podium finish in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday.The 22-year-old clocked 1 minute 5.90 seconds to finish third, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita, who won gold in a Games-record time of 58.22 seconds, and China's Chuanzhen Sun, who took silver in 58.70 seconds.Nandal's latest medal added to his earlier bronze finishes in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. He became one of India's standout performers in para swimming, matching compatriot Ravi Budigina's three-medal haul at the Games, which comprised two silver medals and a bronze.Born blind due to optic nerve failure, Nandal grew up in a sports-oriented family in Rohtak, Haryana. His father had played hockey at the national level, and sport became part of his life from an early age.At four, Nandal moved to Delhi and joined the National Association for the Blind, where he learnt Braille. He initially took up judo and went on to win medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021.The change opened a new chapter in his sporting journey, as he quickly progressed from domestic competitions to the international stage.Nandal achieved a significant milestone in 2024 when he became the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.A political science graduate from the University of Delhi's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, he continued to build his experience against international opposition. In 2025, he reached two finals at the World Para Swimming Championships in Singapore.At the Asian Para Games, Nandal began his medal-winning run on Tuesday, clocking 5:10.91 to secure bronze in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event. He followed it up with another third-place finish in the 100m breaststroke before completing his hat-trick in the 100m freestyle on Friday.The S11 classification is for swimmers with visual impairment, including those with very low visual acuity or no light perception.Nandal's three-medal campaign in Japan marks another milestone in his progress as an Indian para-swimmer and adds to his growing experience at major international competitions.
Article Summary: Himanshu Nandal completes hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games 2026. The 22-year-old finished third in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday. Nandal is the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.

NEW DELHI: Thulasimathi Murugesan produced a memorable triple-medal performance at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Friday, winning gold and two silver medals as India's para-badminton contingent enjoyed a productive day in Aichi-Nagoya.The 24-year-old Paris Paralympics silver medallist capped her campaign with gold in the women's doubles SL3-SU5 event, partnering Manasi Joshi to defeat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final. The Indian pair wrapped up the contest in just 28 minutes.Thulasimathi had earlier settled for silver in the women's singles SU5 final, losing 18-21, 11-21 to China's Yang. She then teamed up with Nitesh Kumar in the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final, but the Indian combination went down 21-11, 19-21, 14-21 to Indonesia's Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani.Nitesh, the Paris Paralympic champion, enjoyed a successful day of his own, winning gold in the men's singles SL3 event before adding mixed doubles silver with Thulasimathi.The 31-year-old defeated compatriot and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in the men's singles final."Last time I was close, I was leading 19-16 in the third set, and then I lost. So this time, winning it and again winning in two sets against Pramod is, of course, very special, and I think it's one of the rarest of the rare things to see," Nitesh said after his victory.Naveen Sivakumar added another gold for India, beating Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 in the men's singles SL4 final. Making his Asian Para Games debut, Naveen completed the win in 36 minutes.Pramod had to settle for silver after winning gold in the 2018 and 2022 editions. India's Nithya Sre Sumathy Sivan also claimed silver in the women's singles SH6 final after losing to China's Li Fengmei.India continued to collect medals across disciplines on Friday. Para shooter Mona Agarwal won her second gold of the Games in the women's 50m rifle 3 Positions SH1 final, setting a world record with 357.5 points. She finished 3.8 points ahead of China's Cuiping Zhang.In para archery, Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi won gold in the men's recurve doubles event. Sandeep claimed the men's 400m T64 title, while Haney won gold in the men's javelin throw F37/38 event.India also added silver medals through Nithya Sre Sumathy Sivan, Pooja Jatyan and Bhawna Choudhary in women's recurve doubles, Parmod Bijarnia in the men's 1500m T46 and Nimisha Suresh in the women's long jump T47. Jehan Madan and Shubham Wadhwa secured bronze in men's doubles para table tennis MD4.India's tally stood at 106 medals — 28 gold, 34 silver and 44 bronze — with the country fourth in the standings. The contingent is chasing its best-ever Asian Para Games haul of 108 medals, achieved at Hangzhou in 2023.

Paris Paralympic silver medallist defeats China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in women's doubles final. Nitesh Kumar wins gold in men's singles SL3 event before adding mixed doubles silver. India's tally stands at 106 medals — 28 gold, 34 silver and 44 bronze — with country fourth in standings.

India's Mona Agarwal continued her golden run at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games, rewriting the world record to clinch her second gold medal of the competition in the women's 50m rifle 3 Positions SH1 final on Friday. The Indian para shooter produced a record score of 357.5 to finish 3.8 points ahead of China's Cuiping Zhang, setting a new World Record and Asian Para Games Record.Mona's latest triumph came after she had already struck gold in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event on the opening day.Mona delivered a composed performance in the 50m rifle 3 Positions SH1 final to secure the gold medal with a world-record score of 357.5. China's Cuiping Zhang finished second to take silver, trailing the Indian by 3.8 points.India's other finalist, Avani Lekhara , narrowly missed out on a podium finish, ending fourth. Avani had been among the leading contenders after the prone position but lost ground during the standing series, which proved decisive in the final standings.Mona had earlier teamed up with Avani for an Indian one-two finish in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event on the opening day.She won gold with a score of 250 after the seventh series, setting an Asian Para Games record and surpassing Avani's previous mark of 249.6 from the 2023 Hangzhou edition.Mona's second gold came as India continued their push to surpass their previous best performance at the Asian Para Games. At the time of reporting, India had collected 103 medals: 27 gold, 33 silver and 43 bronze and stood fourth in the overall standings, with China leading the table with 354 medals.India's record haul at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Para Games was 111 medals.
Article Summary: India's Mona Agarwal wins second gold of 2026 Asian Para Games. She produced a record score of 357.5 to finish 3.8 points ahead of China's Cuiping Zhang. India's other finalist, Avani Lekhara, narrowly missed out on a podium finish, ending fourth.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Thulasimathi clinches silver in women's singles SU5, remains in contention for two more golds
Article Text:
Thulasimathi Murugesan

Thulasimathi falls short against Yang after impressive semi-final comeback

Two more gold medal opportunities await

Who is Thulasimathi Murugesan?

India's Thulasimathi Murugesan added another medal to her growing collection at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games, settling for silver in the women's singles SU5 badminton event after losing to China's Yang Qiuxia in the final on Friday. The 24-year-old, who won silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, went down 18-21, 11-21 against the Chinese shuttler at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium.However, Thulasimathi's campaign is far from over, with the Indian still in contention for two more gold medals in the mixed doubles and women's doubles events. She will look to make amends in the remaining finals as India aim to add to their medal tally.Thulasimathi, currently ranked World No. 2, could not overcome Yang in the title clash, with the Chinese player securing the gold medal in straight games. The Indian had produced a fighting performance in the semi-finals, rallying from a game down to defeat compatriot and World No. 1 Manisha Ramdass 19-21, 21-15, 21-13 and book her place in the final.The silver medal adds to Thulasimathi's impressive record in para-badminton, following her breakthrough performance at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, where she finished runner-up in the women's singles SU5 category.Thulasimathi will have two more chances to finish her campaign on a high.She has partnered Nitesh Kumar to reach the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final, where the Indian duo will face Indonesia's Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani.The Indians booked their place in the final after overcoming China's Li Mingpan and Xiao Zuxian in a hard-fought 42-minute semi-final. Nitesh and Thulasimathi prevailed 21-19, 14-21, 21-17 to secure their place in the gold medal match.Later, Thulasimathi will team up with Manasi Girishchandra Joshi in the women's doubles SL3-SU5 final. The Indian pair will face China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian, giving Thulasimathi another opportunity to challenge for gold against the Chinese shuttler who defeated her in the singles final.Born on April 11, 2002, in Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu, Thulasimathi has established herself as one of India's leading para-badminton players. Her silver medal at the Paris 2024 Paralympics marked a major milestone in her career, while her performances at the Asian Para Games have further strengthened her standing on the international stage.She trains in Hyderabad under coaches Pullela Gopichand and Irfan Sait while pursuing a degree in veterinary science at Namakkal. In recognition of her achievements in para-badminton, including her Paralympic success, she was also honoured with the Arjuna Award.
Article Summary: Thulasimathi Murugesan won silver in the women's singles SU5 event. The 24-year- old lost to China's Yang Qiuxia 18-21, 11-21 in the final. She is still in contention for two more gold medals in the mixed doubles and women's doubles events.

Article Title: Raheem Sterling handed suspended prison sentence after crashing £270,000 Lamborghini while inhaling laughing gas from balloon while driving
Article Text:
Raheem Sterling handed suspended prison sentence and two-year driving ban after dangerous driving while inhaling nitrous oxide in his Lamborghini.

Sterling sentenced after dangerous driving and nitrous oxide offences

Four police reports before Lamborghini crashed into barrier

Arrest, six canisters and admission of a nitrous oxide problem

From four Premier League titles to an uncertain football future

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

FILE - Chelsea's Raheem Sterling during the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Chelsea at the Etihad stadium in Manchester, England, Saturday, Feb. 17, 2024. (AP Photo/Dave Thompson, file)

Raheem Sterling has received a suspended prison sentence after admitting dangerous driving while inhaling nitrous oxide from a balloon during a rush-hour journey that ended with his £270,000 Lamborghini crashing into a roadside barrier. The former England international told the court he had spent 12 days in rehabilitation for his use of the substance, which a judge said had become a maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period in his career.Sterling, 31, was sentenced to 12 months in prison, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court on Wednesday after pleading guilty to dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation.He must also complete 100 hours of unpaid community service and has been disqualified from driving for two years. The court ordered him to pay a victim surcharge of £187 and prosecution costs of £85.In her sentencing remarks, District Judge Kirsty Allman revealed that Sterling had contacted UK Addiction Treatment on June 15 and subsequently entered rehabilitation for 12 days at Banbury Lodge.The judge said nitrous oxide had “become a maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period in his career”.She also referred to Sterling's position as a role model when explaining the sentence.His MBE, charitable work and time spent in rehabilitation were among the mitigating factors considered by the court. Although the sentence does not require him to undergo further therapeutic treatment, the lead therapist at Banbury Lodge believes additional support would be beneficial.Sterling showed little reaction as the sentence was delivered. He arrived wearing a black quarter-zip jumper, white T-shirt and black trousers, and sat in the glass dock with his back against the wall, maintaining eye contact with the judge as she read her remarks.The suspended sentence means he will not serve the 12 months in prison unless he breaches the conditions of the suspension or commits another offence that activates it.The offences took place on May 28, when Sterling drove his black Lamborghini Urus across several roads in Surrey and Hampshire while inhaling nitrous oxide from a balloon.He pleaded guilty in September to dangerous driving on the M25, M3, A327 and Minley Road. He also admitted possessing six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation, failing to provide a specimen and driving dangerously while impaired.Prosecutor Simon Jones told an earlier hearing that police received a series of calls between 7.45am and 8.52am from motorists concerned about the way the Lamborghini was being driven.Witness Christopher Jennings called 999 at 7.49am after travelling alongside Sterling on the M25. Jones told the court that Jennings “was shocked by what he saw” and reported seeing the footballer inhaling from a balloon.Another witness, Fiona Jennings, was driving southbound on the M3 at approximately 8.45am when she noticed the vehicle repeatedly moving between lanes.She described the driving as “absolutely horrendous”, with the Lamborghini “swerving in and out of lanes”, the court heard.Jones told the hearing:“She had genuine concerns the driver might kill someone.”Fiona Jennings initially thought an airbag was involved when she looked across at the driver, but realised she was seeing a large inflated white balloon, with its neck in the driver's mouth.Dashcam footage released by the Crown Prosecution Service showed the Lamborghini switching lanes repeatedly before striking a concrete barrier on the right-hand side of the road and continuing its journey.After leaving the M3 at junction 4a, Sterling travelled along the A327 and completed a loop before losing control shortly after a roundabout. The vehicle left the carriageway and collided with either a road sign or metal gate, causing substantial damage. All four wheels were damaged, leaving the car unable to continue.Four police forces had received reports about the vehicle before the journey ended in the crash.Police body-worn camera footage showed Sterling inside the damaged Lamborghini when officers arrived at approximately 9.15am. Two canisters were visible on his lap as an officer told him: “You can put that down mate.”He was subsequently taken to Basingstoke police investigation centre. According to Jones, Sterling told custody staff that “he had a problem with nitrous oxide”.Sterling completed an impairment test but sought legal advice before deciding whether to provide a blood sample. The prosecutor said that, in the police sergeant's view, he was “deliberately failing to provide a clear answer”.During a later police interview, with legal representation present, Sterling accepted that he had been driving the vehicle but gave no-comment answers when questioned about his driving.At the September hearing, his barrister, Jason Bartfeld KC, accepted that the case fell into the “top category” of dangerous driving because of the prolonged journey and periods of serious impairment.However, the defence disputed the seriousness of the damage caused to the vehicle and argued that there had been “confusion” surrounding Sterling's failure to provide a specimen.The court ultimately considered his guilty pleas, rehabilitation and personal circumstances before imposing the suspended prison sentence.Sterling scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, becoming an important figure under Gareth Southgate. He helped the national team reach the semi-finals of the 2018 World Cup in Russia and the final of Euro 2020, where England lost to Italy on penalties.Born in Kingston, Jamaica, Sterling moved to England as a child and began his football development at Queens Park Rangers before joining Liverpool's academy. He made his senior debut at Anfield and established himself as one of the Premier League's most prominent young attackers.Manchester City signed him in 2015, and he went on to win four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup in 2019 during his time at the Etihad Stadium.He moved to Chelsea in 2022 but struggled to establish a regular place in the side and spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal. After leaving Stamford Bridge, he joined Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term agreement running until the end of the season. He is currently without a club.Sterling was appointed a Member of the Order of the British Empire in the 2021 Queen's Birthday Honours for services to racial equality in sport. He had become a prominent voice against racism and discrimination in football, speaking publicly about abuse directed at players and supporting campaigns promoting equality.His advocacy included speaking out amid controversy over England supporters booing players who took the knee before matches as a gesture against racism and intolerance.The court's decision brings the criminal proceedings over the May incident to sentencing, but Sterling now faces an 18-month suspended sentence, a two-year driving ban and 100 hours of unpaid work.
Article Summary: Sterling, 31, sentenced to 12 months in prison, suspended for 18 months. Former England international pleaded guilty to dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation. He must also complete 100 hours of unpaid community service and has been disqualified from driving for two years. Judge Kirsty Allman said it had become a maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period in his career.

Article Title: New leaked files expose Gianni Infantino’s $20B FIFA plan to lock away World Cup commercial rights for 96 years and offer tens of millions in executive bonuses
Article Text:
FILE PHOTO: FIFA president Gianni Infantino

FIFA planned to transfer World Cup rights for 96 years

Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital emerged as anchor investor

Backstop Letter and Transaction Terms

Infantino faces scrutiny over leadership and political ties

New York Post

Infantino faces first presidential election challenge since 2016

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

FIFA's abandoned private equity proposal was considerably more far-reaching than a conventional investment deal. Documents exchanged with Thrive Capital, the firm founded by Joshua Kushner, reveal plans to transfer the commercial rights to FIFA events into a new $20 billion subsidiary for 96 years, while also allowing for potentially tens of millions of dollars in executive bonuses. The disclosures offer a closer look at a project that became one of the biggest controversies of Gianni Infantino's presidency.Leaked documents reviewed by The Associated Press reveal that FIFA's proposed private equity arrangement would have given a new commercial subsidiary control of the organisation's event rights for almost a century.The plan, known internally as Project Box, involved creating FIFA Forward Enterprises (FFE), a for-profit subsidiary valued at approximately $20 billion. Under the proposed structure, the commercial rights to FIFA events would have been transferred to the company for exploitation over the following 96 years.A FIFA in-house risk assessment, included among the documents reviewed by the AP, described the arrangement in direct terms:“This deal provides for Fifa to create a for-profit subsidiary which would have all the commercial rights for FIFA events transferred to it for commercial exploitation for the next 96 years”.The assessment also revealed that FIFA's own finance officials had limited involvement in developing the transaction.“Were not directly privy to the construction of this transaction,” the document stated of the finance officials.The proposal had been moving towards completion in New York during the weekend of the men's World Cup final on July 19. However, the project only became public nine days after Spain defeated Argentina in the final, triggering a backlash that included criticism from senior figures within FIFA itself.The opposition intensified over concerns about the scale of the proposed transfer, the lack of transparency surrounding negotiations and the concentration of commercial control within a new company. Infantino subsequently withdrew the proposal within days.The leaked papers also shed light on how FIFA selected its prospective investment partner and the negotiations that preceded the proposed agreement.FIFA had initially held discussions with Affinity Partners, the investment firm founded by Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of US President Donald Trump. It subsequently moved towards Thrive Capital, the firm led by Jared's younger brother, Joshua Kushner, as the proposed anchor investor.One of the documents explained why FIFA had not opened a formal tender process, citing “the specific and unique nature of the proposed investment, bilateral and unilateral conversations held with interest from several potential investment sources”.Affinity Partners was referenced in that explanation, indicating that the firm had been among the investment groups involved in discussions before Thrive emerged as the preferred partner.Thrive prepared a document titled, dated July 17, setting out the proposed arrangement with FIFA under the Project Box name. The timing placed the negotiations close to the completion of the men's World Cup, with the new subsidiary potentially becoming a major vehicle for the organisation's commercial operations.The documents also included provisions for a management incentive plan, under which executives at FFE could receive bonuses worth tens of millions of dollars.Those payments would have been determined by the subsidiary's board, which was to be chaired by FIFA's sitting president, Infantino.FIFA defended the proposed structure in a statement, saying:“This is customary for proposed structures of this nature”.The organisation also stressed that the project remained a proposal and would have required approval from its 211 member federations, which effectively own FIFA as a Switzerland-based non-profit organisation.“FIFA's leadership would only have had leading roles in the board, which would not have led to any additional remuneration,” the governing body said.The distinction was significant because the documents outlined potential executive bonuses within the subsidiary, while FIFA maintained that its own leadership would not receive additional remuneration through their board positions.The controversy surrounding Project Box has added to existing concerns about Infantino's leadership style and his relationship with the Trump administration.His ties to the US president have already attracted criticism, particularly over FIFA's decision to create a peace prize and its handling of disciplinary rules at the World Cup. One issue concerned the waiver of a mandatory one-match suspension for United States forward Folarin Balogun.The proposed private equity arrangement intensified concerns among senior figures in European football and officials in Japan, where questions have been raised about FIFA's governance and the extent to which major decisions are being developed within Infantino's inner circle.The leaked documents were first reported by theon Monday. Their disclosure also comes amid a wider dispute between FIFA and UEFA , which has been seeking access to records relating to the proposed commercial rights sell-off.UEFA recently secured a legal victory in Manhattan after a judge rejected FIFA's attempt to block the release of the documents. The European governing body had filed court papers in August as part of a broader effort to challenge Infantino's presidency, including the possibility of a criminal complaint against him personally in Switzerland over alleged financial mismanagement.Those allegations remain separate from the disclosures about Project Box, and the leaked papers do not by themselves establish wrongdoing.The latest disclosures arrive as Infantino prepares for his first contested presidential election since taking charge of FIFA in 2016.Two opponents are campaigning against him ahead of the March 18 vote in Morocco: Philippe Diallo of France and Kohzo Tashima of Japan. Infantino is nevertheless widely expected to secure another term.The election will take place against the backdrop of growing scrutiny over how FIFA conducts its commercial and governance affairs, with the abandoned private equity plan providing opponents and critics with a significant example of the concerns surrounding his administration.The proposed FFE structure would have placed FIFA's event-related commercial rights inside a separate for-profit company for 96 years, with a potential valuation of $20 billion and an executive incentive programme worth tens of millions of dollars. FIFA ultimately withdrew the proposal, but the documents now provide a more detailed account of how far the negotiations had progressed before the plan collapsed.
Article Summary: FIFA's abandoned private equity proposal was considerably more far-reaching than a conventional investment deal. Documents exchanged with Thrive Capital, the firm founded by Joshua Kushner, reveal plans to transfer the commercial rights to FIFA events into a new $20 billion subsidiary for 96 years. The proposal had been moving towards completion in New York during the weekend of the men's World Cup final on July 19.

Article Title: Kalyan Chaubey back in AIFF electoral college after Karnataka nomination cleared
Article Text:
AIFF President Kalyan Chaubey. (ANI)

New Delhi:

How Karnataka State Football Association (KSFA) changed its nomination:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

All India Football Federation (AIFF) president Kalyan Chaubey has found a place in the electoral college after the Electoral Officer approved Karnataka State Football Association’s request to replace Hanif Mohammed due to ill health. The development clears a crucial hurdle for the incumbent president ahead of the December 20 elections.In the electoral college published on Wednesday, Chaubey was listed as Karnataka’s representative alongside NA Haris, the Karnataka FA president and AIFF's vice president.Chaubey's candidature to become president again had taken a hit after his name was withdrawn by the Daman and Diu Football Association. It had created question marks over his participation in the election process.The KSFA had sought approval to alter its representation after the electoral college was initially finalised. The request was accepted by Electoral Officer Rajeev Sharma, who allowed the association to replace Hanif Mohammed with Chaubey.The change followed Hanif's written request to withdraw from the electoral college on medical grounds.The KSFA subsequently sought the substitution, with the Electoral Officer accepting the request after examining the circumstances and the applicable provisions governing changes to delegates.The Karnataka association's request had raised questions over whether a change sought after the prescribed deadline would be permitted.The electoral officer's order cited provisions that allow a member association to nominate its representative, while also making clear that any alteration to the electoral college after the stipulated deadline requires approval. The request was ultimately allowed, with the withdrawal accepted and Chaubey's inclusion approved.The development also brings an interesting political dynamic into the AIFF election. Haris is a Congress politician, while Chaubey has political affiliations with the BJP. The two were part of the leadership that emerged after the 2022 elections, when Chaubey defeated former India captain Bhaichung Bhutia to become AIFF president.Chaubey's presidency has come under scrutiny in recent weeks. Former India internationals, including Bhaichung Bhutia, have sought the intervention of Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, raising concerns about the functioning of the federation and the direction of Indian football ahead of the election.With the electoral college now finalised and Chaubey's inclusion confirmed, attention shifts to the contest for the AIFF's top position. The federation's elections are scheduled to be held in New Delhi on December 20.November 15: The draft electoral college lists N.A. Haris and Hanif Mohammed as Karnataka State Football Association's representatives.November 15: Daman and Diu Football Association withdraws Kalyan Chaubey's nomination as an AIFF election voter, retaining Walter Pereira and Altamash Shaikh as its delegates.November 16: Hanif Mohammed writes to the KSFA Honorary General Secretary, seeking withdrawal of his name from the AIFF electoral college on medical grounds, citing physical and mental stress as well as long-distance travel.November 18 (1:58 pm): KSFA president NA Haris forwards an official request to the Electoral Officer, seeking approval under Article 4.2 of Schedule III to nominate himself and Kalyan Chaubey as the association's representatives.November 18 (4:27 pm): The Electoral Officer's office asks KSFA to submit a medical certificate supporting Hanif's withdrawal.November 19: KSFA submits a medical certificate dated November 14 from Dr Pankaj Singhai, Consultant Physician, Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru. The certificate advises Hanif to avoid long-distance travel and stress and to take rest.November 24: The Electoral Officer approves KSFA's request, accepts Hanif's withdrawal and permits Kalyan Chaubey to replace him as the association's representative, alongside N.A. Haris.November 25: The revised electoral college is published, listing N.A. Haris and Kalyan Chaubey as Karnataka's two representatives for the AIFF elections.
Article Summary: All India Football Federation (AIFF) president Kalyan Chaubey has found a place in the electoral college. The Electoral Officer approved Karnataka State Football Association’s request to replace Hanif Mohammed due to ill health. The development clears a crucial hurdle for the incumbent president ahead of the December 20 elections.

Article Title: Hours after reported Ben Shelton breakup, Trinity Rodman pulls out of USA’s CONCACAF W Championship roster
Article Text:
FILE - Washington Spirit forward Trinity Rodman in action during the second half of an NWSL soccer match against the Portland Thorns FC, on March 13, 2026, in Washington. (AP Photo/Terrance Williams, File)

Rodman ruled out of CONCACAF W Championship

Nov 21, 2026; Washington, District of Columbia, USA; Washington Spirit forward Trinity Rodman (2) reacts after a collision in the first half against the Kansas City Current during the 2026 NWSL Championship game at Audi Field. Mandatory Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images

Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman reportedly end relationship

Daily Mail

Ben shelton and trinity rodman

From courtside support to the demands of two sporting careers

Soccer player Trinity Rodman watches her boyfriend Ben Shelton, of the United States, compete against Frances Tiafoe, of the United States, during the men's singles semifinals of the U.S. Open tennis championships Friday, Sept. 11, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Frank Franklin II)

Us Weekly

Trinity Rodman was preparing for another international assignment after a demanding NWSL season, but her plans took an unexpected turn just hours after reports emerged that she and tennis star Ben Shelton had called time on their relationship. The Washington Spirit forward now faces another development that has put her upcoming USWNT campaign in doubt.Trinity Rodman has withdrawn from the United States squad for the 2026 CONCACAF W Championship, taking place in Texas from November 27 to December 5, 2026, after sustaining what US Soccer described as a minor shoulder injury.The federation announced that the 24-year-old would not be part of the 23-player squad for the tournament window in Texas. Head coach Emma Hayes has called up Gotham FC forward Jaedyn Shaw, who was born in Frisco, Texas, to replace her.Rodman injured her shoulder in the fifth minute of the NWSL Championship final on Saturday, November 21, following an aerial collision with Kansas City Current defender Laney Rouse. She continued playing despite the problem and eventually scored a stoppage-time goal for the Washington Spirit, who lost the final 2-1.The forward's decision to withdraw allows her to recover from the injury rather than risk aggravating it during international duty. Her removal comes after an eventful weekend in which she played through the shoulder problem, scored in the championship defeat and was subsequently ruled out of the national team's plans.Rodman's withdrawal was announced hours after thereported that she and Shelton had separated, ending a relationship that became public in March 2025.The pair had become one of American sport's most recognisable young couples, regularly appearing at each other's matches and making efforts to spend time together despite demanding schedules. However, according to the newspaper, their professional commitments and constant travel eventually made the relationship difficult to maintain.The outlet also reported that the couple remain close despite the split.Their schedules had often required them to travel considerable distances to support one another. Shelton, 24, spends much of the year competing on the ATP Tour, while Rodman's commitments with the Washington Spirit and the US women's national team have kept her travelling across the United States and internationally.The timing of their reported separation was notable: Shelton lost his ATP Finals semi-final to Carlos Alcaraz in Turin on Saturday, while Rodman and the Spirit were beaten in the NWSL Championship on the same evening.Shelton was subsequently seen at Madison Square Garden on Sunday for the New York Knicks' game against the Indiana Pacers. He attended without Rodman, sitting alongside actress Inde Navarette.Rodman and Shelton first attracted attention as a couple in March 2025, initially hinting at their relationship through a TikTok trend before making it public.Their support for each other's careers was visible throughout the following months. Rodman became a regular presence in Shelton's player box during the US Open in September and had also travelled to support him at other tournaments, including Wimbledon in May 2025.On one occasion, she made a particularly demanding journey to watch him compete. After playing an NWSL match in Washington on the day of one of Shelton's US Open appearances, Rodman left the capital almost immediately after the final whistle to reach New York. She was later seen in tears at Arthur Ashe Stadium following Shelton's defeat by Alexander Zverev.Shelton also made time to support Rodman, including after the Washington Spirit's NWSL Championship defeat, when footage showed him consoling her as she cried on the sidelines.In September, Shelton spoke openly about the difficulties of maintaining a relationship while both athletes were pursuing demanding professional careers. Speaking to, he said:“It is really difficult. I think what a lot of people don't see is when we actually do have time or a couple of days off, we're so exhausted that it's tough to do anything. It is tough to make time.”He continued:“Sometimes I leave these tournaments and I'm a bit of a zombie. I'm not the most fun person to be around. But we make a lot of sacrifices for our sport. I'd say both of us are chasing things for our sport. We're not where we want to be yet, we're not in our primes. So this is kind of crunch time.“This is going to be the hardest, most grueling time in our relationship, from my perspective. None of it is easy. But being able to have someone to lean on who's such an elite athlete and doing things at a really high level as well, it helps in so many ways.”
Article Summary: Trinity Rodman has withdrawn from the United States squad for the 2026 CONCACAF W Championship. The 24-year-old sustained a minor shoulder injury in the NWSL Championship final on Saturday, November 21. She continued playing despite the problem and eventually scored a stoppage-time goal for the Washington Spirit, who lost the final 2-1. Rodman's withdrawal was announced hours after thereported that she and tennis star Ben Shelton had separated.

Article Title: NorthEast United, SC Delhi share spoils on ISL’s debut in Imphal
Article Text:
Antonio Moyano (Pic credit: NEUFC)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Manipur fans were treated to some end-to-end football as NorthEast United FC and SC Delhi played out an exciting 1-1 draw on Indian Super League ’s debut in the football-loving state.The sharing of honours at the sold-out Khuman Lampak Stadium in Imphal meant that there was no change in their positions in the table as NEUFC stayed in third spot, with 12 points from seven matches, while SC Delhi were still a rung below with nine points from their seven games. To the surprise of the fans who packed Khuman Lampak on a chilly Tuesday evening, carrying banners and wearing the jerseys of the club from their region, the visitors began the match with gusto and created one attack after another in NEUFC half.And it did not take them long to convert one of the opportunities, courtesy of the skills of Mohammed Aimen in front of goal in the sixth minute. Receiving the ball after a rebound just outside the box, the 23-year-old cut in between two NEUFC defenders and curled in a brilliant shot that beat the leaping Gurmeet Singh and swerved into the right corner.Delhi could have increased their lead soon after as Aimen was exceptional down the left and near the goal, to the disappointment of the Imphal crowd.Even as NEUFC tried to press for an equaliser, Nduka Junior and Ashutosh Mehta kept on doggedly guarding the Delhi defence.But the packed house in the Manipur capital came alive in the 29th minute as a chip from Nikhil Barla from outside the box, perfectly timed, left the until-then solid Delhi defence ball-watching.Moyano took time to receive the ball in front of an open goal and left goalkeeper Nora Fernandez with no chance as his shot thumped into the left corner of the goal.It was their ninth goal from open play this season and made the cheers around the venue even louder.The equaliser slowed down the pace of the game as Delhi tried to regroup while not letting NEUFC take advantage of their new-found confidence. While there were a few half-chances for the Highlanders, the game stayed level at half-time.Delhi seemed to have regained their lead soon after the change of ends as Lalrinliana Hnamte was declared offside by the assistant moments after the referee had deemed his shot a goal.
